name: Mythic Europe
description: The magical and medieval world in which Ars Magica sagas are set, full of wonder and supernatural forces.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The organization of Hermetic magi; an apprentice must pass the Gauntlet and swear the Oath of Hermes to join it.

name: House Tremere
description: Hermetic House named in the book's trademark notice.

name: Doissetep
description: Hermetic covenant named in the trademark notices.

name: Grimgroth
description: Named in the book's trademark notice as a property of the Order of Hermes setting.

name: Calebais
description: The Broken Covenant of Calebais, an adventure site that adolescent apprentices and grogs might stumble upon.

name: House Bonisagus
description: Hermetic House whose magi may take another magus' apprentice, subject to House rules; a sample apprentice belongs to it.

name: Bonisagus
description: Founder whose achievements underpin Hermetic magic, though magic remains unpredictable despite them.

name: House Jerbiton
description: Hermetic House to which the magus Aurulentus belongs.

name: House Verditius
description: Hermetic House for which the book provides a sample apprentice.

name: Ex Miscellanea
description: Hermetic House including the lineage of Pralix, whose magi are good at detecting Gifted individuals.

name: Lineage of Pralix
description: Ex Miscellanea lineage whose magi have the Comprehend Magic Virtue and seek Gifted hedge wizards to bring into the Order.

name: Pralix
description: Founder of the Ex Miscellanea lineage whose members inherit Comprehend Magic.

name: Thebes Tribunal
description: Tribunal that, unlike most, has a dedicated branch of servants searching for Gifted apprentices.

name: Rhine Tribunal
description: Tribunal where Durenmar lies; Odo of Cheriton travels mostly in it and Normandy.

name: Normandy Tribunal
description: Tribunal in which Odo of Cheriton travels collecting animal tales.

name: Durenmar
description: Covenant where the Bonisagus magus Petrus Virilis lives.

name: Aurulentus
description: Magus of House Jerbiton, several of whose forefathers were Gifted.

name: Petrus Virilis
description: Bonisagus magus at Durenmar, all of whose offspring have been Gifted.

name: Merlin
description: Legendary figure who as a child saw the dragons battling underground beneath Vortigern's castle.

name: King Vortigern
description: Legendary king whose castle building was prevented by battling dragons discovered by the child Merlin.

name: Uther Pendragon
description: Legendary king for whom Merlin's childhood deed prepared the way.

name: King Arthur
description: Legendary king cited as a famous example of a hero with an exciting childhood.

name: Herakles
description: Legendary hero cited for dangerous childhood stories.

name: Cú Chulainn
description: Legendary hero cited for dangerous childhood stories.

name: Aesop
description: Pagan writer who gave a threefold division of the ages of man and author of animal fables popular in 1220.

name: Hesiod
description: Pagan writer who mentioned four ages of man.

name: Hippocrates
description: Author of the most popular division of the seven ages of man.

name: St Augustine
description: Christian writer who validated Hippocrates' seven ages of man.

name: St Ambrose
description: Christian writer who validated Hippocrates' seven ages of man.

name: Peter Abelard
description: Philosopher quoted on marriage and children being inconsistent with study.

name: Odo of Cheriton
description: Clerk wandering Mythic Europe collecting animal stories for sermons, who may visit a covenant to interview a child.

name: St Francis of Assisi
description: Preaching friar whom the Merchant's Son sample character hopes to emulate.

name: Satan
description: Said to lay an easy snare for the young and innocent.

name: Eleanor
description: Example seven-year-old character with Magic Sensitivity who incurs an uncontrolled Turbulence of gushing tears.

name: Rufus
description: Example character who takes Inherited Virtue: Large to have a growth spurt around age 10.

name: The Church
description: Christian institution requiring baptism with three sponsors and forbidding abandonment of children.

name: Mongols
description: Invaders mentioned jokingly as a threat no four-year-old would be asked to stop.

name: Dream Witches
description: Group described in an insert of the book.

name: Muspelli
description: Non-Hermetic tradition whose childhoods the book does not specifically address.

name: Learned Magicians
description: Non-Hermetic magical tradition mentioned as also having had childhoods.

name: Diabolist
description: Infernal practitioner, one of the non-Hermetic traditions named.

name: Spirit Votary
description: Non-Hermetic tradition named among those not covered in detail.

name: Faerie Doctor
description: Non-Hermetic tradition named among those not covered in detail.

name: Hedge Wizard
description: Non-Hermetic magician; Pralixians seek Gifted hedge wizards, and a hedge wizard might steal a Gifted baby.

name: Magus
description: Hermetic wizard of the Order of Hermes who trains apprentices.

name: Apprentice
description: Gifted student of a Hermetic magus, trained for about 15 years before the Gauntlet.

name: Grog
description: Low-level character type; young grogs may have up to three points of Virtues and Flaws.

name: Companion
description: Character type; young companions may have up to ten points of Virtues and Flaws.

name: Covenfolk
description: Inhabitants of a covenant, whose children have Son of Covenfolk status.

name: Parens
description: The magus who trains an apprentice, Opens her Arts and is legally responsible for her.

name: Noble Child
description: Sample six-year-old companion, a reckless noble's son prophesied to die by fire, with inherited Skinchanger and Great Dexterity.

name: Foundling Child
description: Sample seven-year-old Gifted orphan apprentice with a knack for books and an inherited Flexible Formulaic Magic.

name: Blacksmith's Son
description: Sample seven-year-old grog, a bully with Magic Sensitivity and No Sense of Direction.

name: Urchin
description: Sample eleven-year-old grog, daughter of a branded outlaw living on city streets who aims to lead a gang of child thieves.

name: Merchant's Son
description: Sample thirteen-year-old companion obsessed with saints' lives, hoping to gain True Faith and become a preaching friar.

name: Apprentice of House Bonisagus
description: Sample eight-year-old girl just accepted into House Bonisagus, raised in the woods, with Apt Student.

name: Divine
description: Realm of Power; baptism and similar rites cancel non-Divine supernatural effects on a child.

name: Infernal
description: Realm of Power; Infernal animals may want a snack of an infant; Hermetic magic has limits against it.

name: Faerie
description: Realm of Power; faerie animals rarely miss a chance to interact with children.

name: Magic
description: Realm of Power; magic animals are curious and Turbulences count as a magic power.

name: The Gift
description: The innate magical ability required for Hermetic magic, which carries negative social penalties and may appear at birth or later.

name: Ages of Man
description: Medieval division of the life cycle; the first three ages, each seven years, are infantia, pueritia and adolescentia.

name: Infantia
description: Infancy, the age of man from birth to age 7.

name: Pueritia
description: Childhood, the age of man from 8 to 14, when most apprentices are found.

name: Adolescentia
description: Adolescence, the age of man from 15 to 21 and the core of Hermetic apprenticeship.

name: Turbulence
description: An uncontrolled magical outburst of a Gifted child's Gift caused by strong emotion or a botched magical activity.

name: Transitions of Maturation
description: Three liminal stages (ages 8, 15 and 21) during which a young character may exchange Virtues and Flaws of equal value.

name: Inherited Virtues and Flaws
description: Virtues or Flaws chosen at creation that have not yet manifested but must materialize by age 21.

name: Child Virtues and Flaws
description: New type of Virtue and Flaw reflecting childhood traits that must be exchanged by adulthood.

name: Standard Apprenticeship
description: Benchmark model of a 15-year apprenticeship yielding about 240 experience points and 120 spell levels.

name: Aging Chart
description: Table giving Characteristic and Size modifiers for characters by age.

name: Example Childhoods
description: Ability packages (Athletic, Border, Covenant Bred, Exploring, Feral, Fighting, Mischievous, Shy, Social, Traveling, Wilderness) for spending 45 experience points by age 5.

name: Cantations
description: Low-level formulaic spells that give child apprentices the chance to cast formulaic magic.

name: Bellum
description: Magical game played by adolescent apprentices and young magi to practice Arcane Abilities.

name: Gauntlet
description: Test that ends Hermetic apprenticeship, determining if an apprentice is ready to swear the Oath and become a magus.

name: Oath of Hermes
description: Oath sworn by a new magus to join the Order of Hermes.

name: Opening the Arts
description: Season-long procedure by which a parens unlocks an apprentice's ability to use Hermetic magic and legally binds her to him.

name: Hermetic Law
description: Law of the Order requiring 15 years of apprenticeship with at least one season of teaching per year; faulty Opening of Arts is a low crime.

name: Code of Hermes
description: The law of the Order, which forbids scrying on another magus with Intellego Vim.

name: Low Crime
description: Class of Hermetic offense, e.g. abandoning an apprentice or deliberately including Deficiencies when Opening the Arts.

name: Scrying
description: Magical spying on a magus; using Intellego Vim on another magus counts as scrying and is forbidden.

name: Marched
description: Hunted down and slain as an outcast magus; an abandoned apprentice may be treated like a Marched magus.

name: Birth Apparitions
description: Visions or supernatural beings that appear at the birth of important people with realm-linked Virtues or Flaws.

name: Baptism
description: Christian sacrament that cancels non-Divine supernatural effects on a child and drives out possessing spirits, without affecting the Gift.

name: Brit Milah
description: Jewish ritual circumcision and naming eight days after a boy's birth, with the same divine effect as baptism.

name: Adhan
description: The Islamic call to prayer whispered into a newborn's ear during ritual purification.

name: Godsibs
description: The three baptismal sponsors (godfathers and godmothers) required by the Church for each child.

name: Aura
description: Supernatural area strength that adds to the roll to incur a Turbulence.

name: Regio
description: Supernatural region; Magic Sensitivity draws the Blacksmith's Son toward regiones.

name: Twilight
description: Temporary Twilight is an adult magus' magical crisis, likened to controlling a Turbulence.

name: Warping
description: Magical corruption measured by Warping Score, opposed to Stamina when controlling a Turbulence.

name: Magic Resistance
description: Protection against magic; a Turbulence cannot affect a target with Magic Resistance without Penetration.

name: Might
description: Supernatural creature power score; birth apparitions usually have Might 5 or 10.

name: Sympathetic Magic
description: Use of sympathetic connections to multiply Penetration, including for Turbulences.

name: Invitation Token
description: Token letting a magical being or apprentice work magic within the Aegis of the Hearth; may be given to apprentices.

name: Laboratory
description: The magus' workspace, which apprentices clean and where they assist; children can add to Safety and Aesthetics.

name: Teaching Source Quality
description: Measure of instruction quality; the standard parens generates 13.

name: Exposure
description: Experience gained by an apprentice assisting the parens when not being taught.

name: Confidence
description: Points a player spends to add to rolls, including to force a Turbulence.

name: Animals of Virtue
description: Magical animals described in medieval bestiaries.

name: Aesop's Fables
description: Animal fables popular in 1220 whose supernatural animals can be adapted into adventures.

name: Hedge Magic
description: Non-Hermetic magical traditions; a witch's Hedge Arts may let her take an apprentice.

name: False Gift
description: Infernal counterpart of The Gift which Intellego Vim cannot distinguish from the true Gift.

name: Blood Rights
description: Rules concerning claims on the Gifted children of magi.

name: Scholae Magicae
description: Topic of post-apprenticeship schooling in magic covered by the book.

name: Covenant
description: Hermetic community where apprentices live, work and play; kinder to Gifted children than villages.

name: Laboratory Turbulences
description: Turbulences occurring during laboratory work, covered in the Adolescentia chapter.

name: Hermetic Virtues
description: Virtues relating to Hermetic magic which an apprentice can be taught or acquire, including House Virtues.

name: Free House Virtue
description: House Virtue that an apprentice studying long enough with his parens may acquire.

name: Social Status
description: Category of Virtue or Flaw every character needs; children usually take Son/Daughter of their parent's status.

name: Mitigating Deadly Wounds
description: Optional rule letting a player reduce a wound's severity by accepting a new Flaw.

name: Apprentice
description: Free Social Status Virtue: the character is apprenticed to a Hermetic magus.

name: Orphan
description: Free Social Status Virtue: the child's parents are unknown or deceased.

name: Boundless Energy
description: Minor Child Virtue granting +3 to Fatigue rolls.

name: Deft Characteristic
description: Minor Child Virtue halving the age Characteristic Modifier for one Characteristic.

name: Grows Quickly
description: Minor Child Virtue treating the character as one age category higher for Size.

name: Inconspicuous
description: Minor Child Virtue giving +3 to hide and avoid attention.

name: Protection from Diseases
description: Major Child Supernatural Virtue granting immunity to all diseases from a supernatural agent.

name: Warrior
description: Virtue granting extra experience points, prohibited for characters under 14.

name: Educated
description: Virtue granting extra experience points, prohibited for characters under 14.

name: Skilled Parens
description: Virtue assuming an unusually capable parens (Teaching Source Quality 18-19, Lab Total 50).

name: Large
description: Minor General Virtue increasing Size; may be Inherited to manifest later.

name: Giant-Blooded
description: Virtue increasing Size, making a one-year-old Size -1.

name: Light Touch
description: Virtue a Child Virtue such as Grows Quickly might become.

name: Sharp Ears
description: Virtue a Child Virtue such as Grows Quickly might become.

name: Tough
description: Virtue a Child Virtue such as Grows Quickly might become.

name: Wealthy
description: Virtue granting 20 experience points per year of childhood.

name: Affinity with Ability
description: Virtue affecting experience points, e.g. Affinity in Single Weapon, which must be kept once gained.

name: Affinity with Art
description: Virtue for an Art that is a good choice for Turbulence effects.

name: Puissant Ability
description: Virtue adding to an Ability score; can be replaced during transitions (e.g. Puissant Latin, Puissant Craft).

name: Puissant Art
description: Virtue adding to an Art score; can be replaced during transitions and suits Turbulence effects.

name: Improved Characteristics
description: Virtue adding Characteristic points; can be gained and replaced.

name: Son of Knight
description: Minor Social Status Virtue of a young squire.

name: Son of Covenfolk
description: Free Social Status Virtue for children of covenant inhabitants.

name: Son of Landed Noble
description: Social Status Virtue of the Noble Child sample character.

name: Son of Merchant
description: Social Status Virtue of the Merchant's Son.

name: Son of Craftsman
description: Social Status Virtue of the Blacksmith's Son.

name: Great Dexterity
description: Virtue inherited by the Noble Child, to manifest later.

name: Skinchanger
description: Supernatural Virtue inherited by the Noble Child, to manifest later.

name: Flexible Formulaic Magic
description: Hermetic Virtue inherited by the Foundling Child, to materialize during apprenticeship.

name: Book Learner
description: Virtue of the Foundling Child.

name: Sense Holiness and Unholiness
description: Supernatural Virtue/Ability of the Foundling Child.

name: Intuition
description: Virtue of the Blacksmith's Son.

name: Magic Sensitivity
description: Supernatural Virtue/Ability to sense magic, which draws the Blacksmith's Son toward auras and regiones.

name: Inspirational
description: Virtue of the Urchin.

name: True Faith
description: Virtue the Merchant's Son hopes to gain through veneration of a relic.

name: Luck
description: Virtue of the Merchant's Son, lucky since birth.

name: Relic
description: Virtue: the Merchant's Son found a holy relic.

name: Apt Student
description: Virtue adding to Teaching Source Quality when taught.

name: Second Sight
description: Supernatural Virtue; a child with it might be asked to look for regiones.

name: Premonitions
description: Supernatural Virtue; a child with it might accompany covenant goods to market.

name: Comprehend Magic
description: Supernatural Virtue inherent in the lineage of Pralix, useful for detecting Gifted individuals.

name: Gentle Gift
description: Form of the Gift without social penalty; an infant with it might never be noticed.

name: Peasant
description: Social Status that Son of Peasant becomes on coming of age.

name: Bastard
description: Minor Social Status Flaw: an illegitimate child whose father does not recognize him.

name: Bully
description: Minor Child Personality Flaw: compelled to pick on weaker others (Bully +3).

name: Dependence
description: Minor Child Personality Flaw: uncomfortable without a trusted mentor, -3 when alone.

name: Infatuation
description: Major or Minor Child Story Flaw: romantic attraction to someone with no chance of a relationship.

name: Know-It-All
description: Major or Minor Child Personality Flaw: compelled to show off knowledge and superiority.

name: Late Bloomer
description: Minor Child Flaw: treated as one age category lower on the Aging Chart.

name: Turbulence Prone
description: Major Child Flaw for Gifted characters: must check for turbulence on every potential magical botch.

name: Abandoned Apprentice
description: Major Story Flaw: abandoned by the master mid-training, knowing Hermetic magic but not in the Order.

name: Frail
description: Minor General Flaw giving -3 to Soak.

name: Low Tolerance
description: Minor General Flaw increasing Fatigue and wound penalties and -3 to resist pain.

name: Short of Breath
description: Minor General Flaw giving -3 to Stamina rolls to avoid fatigue.

name: Slow Reflexes
description: Minor General Flaw giving -3 to Initiative when a quick response is needed.

name: Suppressed Gift
description: Major Hermetic Story Flaw: the Gift is temporarily inaccessible, preventing Hermetic magic and Parma Magica.

name: Weak Parens
description: Flaw assuming a weak parens (Teaching Source Quality 8, Lab Total 30).

name: Outlaw
description: Major Social Status Flaw, e.g. for a squire who kills a priest.

name: Small Frame
description: Flaw reducing Size; a child with it stays Size -3 until 12.

name: Dwarf
description: Flaw reducing Size; a Dwarf stays Size -3 until 14.

name: Poor
description: Flaw giving only 10 experience points per year of childhood.

name: Death Prophecy
description: Flaw of the Noble Child, prophesied to die by fire.

name: Feud
description: Flaw of the Noble Child.

name: Ability Block
description: Flaw (Academic) of the Noble Child.

name: Poor Hearing
description: Flaw of the Noble Child.

name: Poor Student
description: Flaw of the Noble Child.

name: Reckless
description: Flaw of the Noble Child.

name: Blatant Gift
description: Flaw: an obvious Gift; such babies are often destroyed or abandoned.

name: Plagued by Supernatural Entity
description: Flaw whose creature appears as a birth apparition.

name: Supernatural Nuisance
description: Flaw with a supernatural attachment that may appear as a birth apparition.

name: No Sense of Direction
description: Flaw of the Blacksmith's Son, who can never find his way home.

name: Daughter of Branded Criminal
description: Social Status Flaw of the Urchin.

name: Dark Secret
description: Flaw: the Merchant's Son knows of his father's illegal business practices.

name: Overconfident
description: Flaw of the Merchant's Son.

name: Obsessed
description: Flaw of the Merchant's Son, obsessed with saints' lives.

name: Soft-Hearted
description: Flaw of the Apprentice of House Bonisagus.

name: Enemies
description: Background Flaw only allowed after an enemy has surfaced in play.

name: Deficient Technique
description: Hermetic Flaw an apprentice gains if the parens' Technique score is below 5 when Opening the Arts.

name: Shared Lab
description: New Laboratory Flaw introduced in the book.

name: Athletics
description: Ability used by young characters, e.g. in example childhoods and sample characters.

name: Brawl
description: Ability used by young characters, e.g. in example childhoods and sample characters.

name: Craft
description: Vocational Ability such as Blacksmith that children may learn from parents.

name: Profession
description: Vocational Ability such as Midwife, Merchant or Forester that children may learn from parents.

name: Artes Liberales
description: Ability used by young characters, e.g. in example childhoods and sample characters.

name: Church Lore
description: Ability used by young characters, e.g. in example childhoods and sample characters.

name: Magic Theory
description: Ability needed by a proper laboratory assistant.

name: Penetration
